title: Model Binding Basics
description: Understand how model binding works in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: **Model binding** automatically maps request data to action method parameters. It can bind from the route, query string, request body, and headers.

When an HTTP request hits your API, ASP.NET Core inspects the route data, query string, headers, and body. It then matches those values to your action parameters by name and type, converting strings to integers, decimals, GUIDs, and complex objects automatically.

terms.definition: The process that converts incoming request data into strongly typed .NET objects that are passed to controller actions.
The origin of data used for binding, such as route, query string, request body, or headers.
A parameter defined on a controller action method that receives data from model binding.
Services that fetch data from specific locations. For example, RouteValueProvider, QueryStringValueProvider, and FormValueProvider.

data.caption: How an ASP.NET Core request reaches an action parameter through model binding.
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[HTTP Request] --> B{Model Binding}
    B -->|Route data| C[FromRoute]
    B -->|Query string| D[FromQuery]
    B -->|JSON body| E[FromBody]
    B -->|Headers| F[FromHeader]
    C --> G[Action Parameter]
    D --> G
    E --> G
    F --> G

data.text: ASP.NET Core applies different default rules based on parameter type. Simple types like int, string, and bool default to [FromQuery]. Complex types such as classes and records default to [FromBody]. You can override either default by adding an explicit attribute.

data.title: Multi-Source Binding
data.content: Combining route, query, and header parameters in a single action.

cards.title: Simple Types
cards.description: int, string, bool, Guid, DateTime, and enums.

cards.title: Complex Types
cards.description: Classes, records, and structs with multiple properties.
cons: Only one complex type per action unless attributed

items.text: Use [FromRoute] for resource identifiers in the URL path
Use [FromQuery] for optional filters, page numbers, and search terms
Use [FromBody] for create and update payloads
Avoid binding more than one complex parameter from the body per action
Rely on [ApiController] automatic 400 responses when ModelState is invalid
Test with missing and malformed values to confirm expected behavior

data.title: Practice Multi-Source Binding
data.description: Create a controller action that binds a route ID, a query search term, and a custom header simultaneously.
steps: Add a new GET endpoint at api/categories/{id}.
Bind a query string parameter named includeInactive using [FromQuery] with a default of false.
Bind a header named X-Tenant-Id using [FromHeader].
Return a 200 OK with the filtered result, or 404 if the category is missing.
data.expectedOutcome: A working endpoint that accepts data from three different binding sources and returns the correct response.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Model binding maps request data to action parameters automatically
Attributes like [FromRoute], [FromQuery], and [FromBody] control the source
Simple types default to query string; complex types default to body
[ApiController] short-circuits invalid ModelState with a 400 response
data.takeaway: Model binding removes manual parsing and keeps your actions clean.
